name: Distress, being shaken (vyathā)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Seeing the fierce form, the three worlds and Arjuna are shaken (pravyathita) (11.20, 11.23); shaken in his inner self he finds neither steadiness nor calm (11.24); the Lord tells him 'do not be distressed' (11.34, 11.49); the dear devotee is 'rid of distress' (gatavyatha) (12.16).
antidotes: the Lord's reassurance and the sight of his gentle form again (11.49–51)

name: Elation (harṣa)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Elation, named with intolerance, fear and agitation as what the dear devotee is free from (12.15); he 'neither rejoices nor hates' (12.17).

name: Intolerance (amarṣa)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Intolerance / indignation, named with elation, fear and agitation as what the dear devotee is free from (12.15).

name: Agitation (udvega)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Agitation: the dear devotee neither disturbs the world nor is disturbed (na udvijate) by it, and is free from elation, intolerance, fear and agitation (12.15).

name: Fear (bhaya)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Fear and fearlessness are among the states of beings from the Lord (10.4); seeing the fierce form Arjuna is shaken with fear, loses his bearings and trembles (11.23–25, 11.35, 11.45); the Lord bids him be free of fear (vyapetabhīḥ) (11.49); the dear devotee is free from fear (12.15).
antidotes: the Lord's reassurance and the sight of his gentle form (11.49–51)

name: Delusion (moha)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Whoever knows the Lord as unborn and beginningless is undeluded (10.3); Arjuna's delusion is gone through the teaching on the self (11.1); he is told not to be bewildered (vimūḍhabhāva) by the terrible form (11.49).
antidotes: knowing the Lord as unborn, beginningless, great lord of the world (10.3)

name: Ignorance veiling knowledge (ajñāna)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The darkness born of ignorance, which the Lord, out of compassion, destroys for his devotees with the shining lamp of knowledge (10.11).
antidotes: the Lord's lamp of knowledge, given to those who worship him with love (10.10–11)

name: Heedlessness (pramāda)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: Arjuna asks forgiveness for what he said to Kṛṣṇa as to a friend, not knowing his greatness, 'through heedlessness or through affection' (11.41–42).

name: Attachment (saṅga)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The one who comes to the Lord is free from attachment (saṅgavarjita) (11.55); the dear devotee is freed from attachment (saṅgavivarjita) (12.18).

name: Aversion (dveṣa)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The dear devotee hates no being (adveṣṭā sarvabhūtānām) (12.13) and neither rejoices nor hates (12.17); the one who comes to the Lord is without enmity toward any being (11.55).

name: The sense of 'mine' (mamatva)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The dear devotee is without 'mine' (nirmama) (12.13).

name: The sense of 'I' (ahaṃkāra)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The dear devotee is without the sense of 'I' (nirahaṅkāra) (12.13).

name: Grief (śoka)
description: Bhagavad Gītā 10–12: The dear devotee neither grieves nor craves (12.17).
